summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Republic of Belarus (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/600), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The United Kingdom's sanctions regime on Belarus, made by the Secretary of State under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018. Its finance part freezes the assets of designated persons, bans making funds or economic resources available to them, and restricts dealing in securities of, lending to and reserve management for the Belarusian state and Belarusian entities; other parts cover trade, aircraft, ships and immigration. A bank screens against the designations, refuses the restricted securities and loan business, relies only on Treasury licences and reports to the Treasury.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Syria (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/792), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The United Kingdom's sanctions regime on Syria, made by the Secretary of State under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018. Its finance part freezes the assets of designated persons, bans making funds or economic resources available to them and bars trading in, or brokering, bonds of the former Assad regime with Syrian credit and financial institutions; other parts cover trade, aircraft and immigration. A bank checks customers and payments against the designations, relies only on Treasury licences and reports to the Treasury.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Venezuela (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/135), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The United Kingdom's sanctions regime on Venezuela, made by the Secretary of State under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018. Its finance part freezes the funds and economic resources of the persons the Secretary of State designates and bans making either available to them or for their benefit; other parts cover trade, immigration and director disqualification. A bank checks customers and payments against the designations, holds what matches frozen, relies only on Treasury licences and reports to the Treasury, once a year too.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Iran (Sanctions) (Nuclear) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/461), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The United Kingdom's sanctions regime on Iran's nuclear programme, made by the Secretary of State under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 and widened in September 2026. Its finance part freezes the assets of designated persons, bans making funds or economic resources available to them or giving them financial messaging services, and bars accounts, correspondent relationships and offices involving Iranian banks and dealings in new Iranian state bonds; other parts cover trade, aircraft, ships and immigration. A bank screens, freezes, shuns Iranian banking links and reports.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Markets in Financial Instruments) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/701), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The Treasury's regulations of 2017 for markets in financial instruments, made beside the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000. Most of them give the FCA and the PRA powers and duties, among them setting position limits in commodity derivatives and removing members of a firm's management body. Directly, they bar anyone, in the United Kingdom or not, from holding a commodity derivative position above a limit the FCA sets by direction. A bank or investment firm trading commodity derivatives keeps its positions within those limits.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Reporting Cryptoasset Service Providers (Due Diligence and Reporting Requirements) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/744), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The Treasury's regulations that apply the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in the United Kingdom from 1 January 2026, made under the Finance Act 2002 and the Finance (No. 2) Act 2023. They bind reporting cryptoasset service providers that the framework's rules subject to reporting here, a bank included where it is one. Such a firm applies the due diligence procedures to its cryptoasset users, keeps records for five years, registers with HMRC, tells reportable users their data goes to HMRC and reports to HMRC each year by 31 May.

summaries.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Mortgage Credit Directive Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/910), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14. Open Government Licence v3.0

text.en: The Treasury's order of 2015 on mortgage credit, which amended the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, the Consumer Credit Act 1974 and orders made under them. Its own Part 3 sets up a register of firms doing consumer buy-to-let mortgage business, supervised by the FCA. A lender, broker or adviser with a Part 4A permission for mortgage or credit activities does consumer buy-to-let mortgage business only once registered, and then meets the requirements of Schedule 2, keeps evidence of compliance and answers the FCA's requests for information.
